presentingComplaint: Two weeks of progressive fatigue, easy bruising and low-grade fever
history: 34-year-old previously well man with a 2-week history of increasing tiredness and breathlessness on exertion, spontaneous bruising over the limbs and gum bleeding while brushing teeth. Reports intermittent low-grade fevers and drenching night sweats over the same period, plus two self-limiting nosebleeds. No overt weight loss but reduced appetite. No prior chemotherapy, radiation, benzene exposure or family history of haematological malignancy. No anticoagulant use.
examination: Pale conjunctivae, scattered ecchymoses and petechiae over both shins and forearms, gingival bleeding and mild gum hypertrophy. No lymphadenopathy; spleen tip just palpable, liver not enlarged. No focal neurological deficit and no neck stiffness. Chest clear, no localising source of infection identified.

labs.peripheral_smear: numerous circulating blasts, some with Auer rods
labs.coagulation: PT/aPTT mildly deranged, fibrinogen low-normal (monitor for DIC)

imaging: Chest X-ray clear; not diagnostic — imaging not required to establish diagnosis
microbiology: Blood cultures sent as febrile; pending. No source identified
finalDiagnosis: Acute leukaemia (acute myeloid leukaemia — blasts with Auer rods)
stewardship: not applicable — non-infective (low-grade fever is common at presentation; empiric antibiotics are indicated only if the patient meets febrile-neutropenia criteria, which is a separate pathway, not treatment of the leukaemia itself)
contraindications: Avoid IM injections and antiplatelet/anticoagulant drugs given severe thrombocytopenia
Platelet transfusion threshold and avoidance of NSAIDs for fever
Allopurinol/rasburicase caution — check G6PD before rasburicase for tumour lysis prophylaxis
edgeCases: Acute promyelocytic leukaemia (APL) variant presents with prominent DIC and bleeding and is a haematological emergency requiring urgent ATRA before genetic confirmation
Pancytopenia without circulating blasts (aleukaemic leukaemia) can mimic aplastic anaemia and needs marrow examination
Hyperleukocytosis (WBC >100) can cause leukostasis with dyspnoea and neurological signs
expectedMaiK: Bicytopenia/pancytopenia with circulating blasts and Auer rods on smear points to acute myeloid leukaemia; this is a haematological emergency requiring urgent marrow examination, tumour-lysis and DIC monitoring, and referral rather than antibiotic treatment.
expectedNextQuestions: Any recent chemotherapy/radiation, benzene or prior myelodysplasia?
Any bleeding from multiple sites or signs suggesting DIC/APL?
Any bone pain, gum infiltration or CNS symptoms?
expectedInvestigations: Urgent bone marrow aspirate and trephine with flow cytometry, cytogenetics and molecular studies
Peripheral blood film review and coagulation screen with fibrinogen (assess for DIC/APL)
Tumour lysis panel — uric acid, potassium, phosphate, calcium, LDH, renal function

investigations: Bone marrow aspirate and trephine with flow cytometry/cytogenetics

regressionAssertions: stewardship tier must be null (non-infective condition)
